title: Hippocampal sharp wave‐ripple: A cognitive biomarker for episodic memory and planning - PMC
abstract:
Alteration of the physiological mechanisms supporting SPW‐Rs leads to their pathological conversion, “p‐ripples,” which are a marker of epileptogenic tissue and can be observed in rodent models of schizophrenia and Alzheimer's Disease. Mechanisms for SPW‐R genesis and function are discussed in this review. © 2015 The Authors Hippocampus Published by Wiley Periodicals, Inc. Keywords: memory, imagining, planning, epilepsy, learning
The SPW‐R has become the first definite biomarker for cognitive operations. Recently, several novel observations have been reported and the retrospective role of SPW‐Rs has been supplemented with ideas about their prospective roles. The goal of this review is twofold. First, it aims to overview the various physiological facets of hippocampal SPW‐Rs (see from Behavioral Correlates and Mechanisms of SPW Generation section to Mechanisms of Ripple Generation sections) and considers the evidence and caveats for their role in memory.

Similarly to the behavioral functions of the hippocampal SPW‐Rs (see Ripples and Fast Gamma/Epsilon Oscillations section), sharp waves in the olfactory system may represent a key offline mechanism to consolidate olfactory memory (Wilson, 2010; Narikiyo et al., 2014).

The original trace (top) and the band‐pass filtered sweep disclosing the ripple oscillation (bottom) are shown. Three episodes of clustered SPW‐Rs containing two to three events are presented.
